key_insight: Wall-induced anisotropy is transferred from the turbulent flow to inertial settling particles and can persist down to scales that are otherwise nearly isotropic, altering scale-wise particle energetics.
engineering_relevance: This helps improve reduced-order and continuum models for particle dispersion and two-way coupling in wall-bounded multiphase flows, especially when settling and inertia are important.
method: Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian direct numerical simulations of inertial particles in a turbulent wall-bounded flow.
Derived an exact, unclosed scale-wise conservation law for particle-phase energetics.
Used an asymptotic argument to interpret how turbulence intensity, inertia, and settling shape anisotropic energy transfer.
evidence_signal: The conclusions are supported by coupled DNS at moderate Reynolds number, with scale-wise analysis of quasi-streamwise and vertical particle fluctuations.
watch_item: The conservation law is exact but unclosed, so practical models will need closure assumptions and may be sensitive to wall effects and moderate-Reynolds-number limits.
paper_title: Development and application of a multiphase Lagrangian structure function model in anisotropic turbulence
